task: T1: extract the transport-agnostic dispatch core in scripts/dispatch/dispatcher.py. Define a new module-level function `dispatch(intent, event_id, *, ledger_path, image, namespace)` that takes an ALREADY-PARSED intent mapping — never a chat string — and performs the whole sequence in order: if the event id is already in the ledger, return without launching anything; otherwise render the Job, launch it, record the event id, and return the same result mapping `handle_event` returns today. Then rewrite `handle_event(text, event_id, *, ledger_path, image, namespace)` so that its entire body is: parse the intent from the text; if there is none, return the no-intent result; otherwise return the result of calling `dispatch`. After this change `handle_event` must NOT itself call the Job renderer, the launcher, the ledger reader or the ledger writer — it calls the parser and it calls `dispatch`, and nothing else. There must be exactly one copy of the dedupe-render-launch-record sequence in the module, because that sequence is the idempotency mechanism and two copies of it will drift. The externally visible behaviour of `handle_event` must not change at all: same arguments, same result keys, same ordering guarantees. Do not add an optional text parameter to `dispatch` — that would preserve the weld under a new name and let a future transport slip a chat string through.
